sn35.245:6.1: _Kiṁsuka_ should be resolved _kiṁ-suka_ (“what parrot?”) rather than _kiṁ-su-ka_ (“what’s it?”), as shown by the Sanskrit spelling _kiṁśuka_. In Ritusaṁhāra 6.22, a poem sometimes attributed to Kalidasa, the comparison to a parrot is made explicit. In Pali it is also referred to as _palāsa_, in which case I use flame-of-the-forest. It is *Butea monosperma*, whose distinctive flower keels resemble the curled beak of a parrot. The simile is further drawn out in the Kiṁsukopama Jātaka ([ja248]()).

sn35.245:7.4: The flowers can resemble scraps of meat. Visuddhimagga 196.5–15 tells of a foolish jackal who danced in joy on finding a meat-bearing tree.
